scope: FP32 reproduction diagnosis only; PTQ/ACQ unchanged

findings.observation: The author detection forwards select i+1 in target_layers. Our [layer-1] timm indices select the same block outputs. Real block hooks confirm all five levels for all three encoders.

The local adapter passes norm=True for every encoder. The upstream DINOv2 and DINOv3 detection forwards return raw block outputs, with final LayerNorm commented out. This is not canceled by later cosine normalization: LayerNorm changes directions, not only scalar norms. CLIP does require its post-LayerNorm and projection.
findings.causal_limit: A paired 15-epoch experiment on 510 auxiliary samples and four target categories changes baseline zero/four-shot AUROC from 89.58/94.83 to 91.26/96.45 when using raw features. With executable scoring the changes are 94.54/98.68 to 94.22/98.73. This demonstrates an effect but not a uniform improvement or the dominant four-shot headline cause.

findings.observation: CLIP has one prefix token; DINOv2-R and DINOv3 each have five. All storage/register tokens are excluded. Both CLIP global and patch features receive the learned projection once; QuickGELU is inside the transformer MLP, not an extra activation on projected outputs.

The paper declares lambda_f=lambda_p=0.5. The released industrial executable uses lambda_f=0.8, lambda_p=0.1 for zero-shot and 0.5 for few-shot; it also applies sigmoid scale 15 with zero/reference offsets 0.4/0.3. Reference smoothing precedes its sigmoid. Interpolation uses align_corners=False, and image peak extraction follows the resize to 256. Local baseline uses paper-default fusion, no sigmoid, align_corners=True, and pools before that final resize.
findings.causal_limit: Prespecified ablations use unchanged heads, features and reference images. Matching a published executable is not proof of the unpublished paper-run configuration.

findings.observation: Local augmentation randomly mixes grid mosaics and positive grid crops for both auxiliary datasets, after first resizing each image. The author executable uses VisA mask-centered jittered crops with category crop-box history for normal images, and MVTec mosaics with rotated companion images and variable tile geometry. Photometric transforms precede the final resize in the author pipeline. Matching gate probabilities therefore did not reproduce the realized author training distribution.
findings.causal_limit: Recipe discrepancy is confirmed; its isolated accuracy contribution has not been measured.

findings.observation: Normal-only per-category pool and seeds are valid, but local randperm samples without replacement while the author uses randint with replacement. All 45 MVTec category/seed four-shot selections differ. Equal seed values alone do not reproduce the author reference sets.
findings.bounded_accuracy_effect: On bottle/cable/carpet/hazelnut with unchanged DINOv2 head/features and executable scoring, the local-pool with-replacement algorithm changes four-shot image AUROC 98.52 to 98.07. This is a local-pool RNG comparison, not a comparison to unavailable original author manifests.

findings.observation: Upstream test.py explicitly computes arithmetic category means, as our report does. Independent sklearn checks agree with anomalib image and pixel AUROC/AP on ordered, tied, and partially ordered fixtures. Pooled AUROC is not recoverable by averaging category AUROCs and is not the author executable's reporting convention.

Image cross-entropy, focal gamma 2 with smoothing 1e-5, and summed normal/anomaly linear Dice with smoothing 1 match the factual upstream declarations. Both implementations resize probabilities, but local training loss uses align_corners=True while upstream head interpolation defaults to False. A fixed synthetic fixture gives losses 1.91106 versus 1.99773. All six historical loss curves are finite and improve. This rules out obvious divergence, not training equivalence.
